 Toyota recalls more than 228,000 vehicles over seat back safety concerns 
 The recall impacts certain 2022 through 2026 Toyota Sienna Hybrid vehicles. 
 By Danielle Abreu • 
 Published 1 hour ago • 
 Updated 56 minutes ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 An auto safety recall is issued when a vehicle or its equipment poses a safety risk or fails to meet federal standards.
 Toyota is recalling more than 228,000 vehicles due to a potential issue with the second-row seat backs, which may fail to stay secured in the event of a crash.
 The recall impacts certain 2022 through 2026 Toyota Sienna Hybrid vehicles.
 Stream NBC4 newscasts for free right here, right now.
   WATCH HERE 
 According to a recall notice posted by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the second-row seat backs could disengage from its locked position in a crash, failing ​to properly ​restrain ⁠passengers and increasing the risk of injury.
 Dealers will update the supplemental restraint system (SRS) electronic control unit (ECU) software.
 For vehicles equipped with the "Mobility as a Service" (MaaS) package, dealers will replace the two second-row seat backs free of charge.
 Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed Dec. 7.
